questions.title: How does the Fetch API work?
questions.answer: The Fetch API provides a Promise-based interface for making HTTP requests. fetch() returns a Promise that fulfills with a Response object when a response becomes available.
questions.underTheHood: The browser performs the network operation and resolves or rejects the associated Promise according to the Fetch API's rules.
pitfalls: HTTP error statuses do not automatically reject fetch().
Response bodies are streams and are generally consumed once.
Network errors and HTTP errors must be distinguished.
followUps: What is the difference between fetch and XMLHttpRequest?

questions.title: What is AbortController?
questions.answer: AbortController provides a way to signal cancellation to APIs that support AbortSignal, including fetch().
questions.underTheHood: An AbortController owns a signal. Calling abort() marks the signal as aborted and notifies operations observing it.
pitfalls: AbortController only affects operations that support its signal.
Aborting a request does not guarantee that the server stopped processing it.
Abort errors should be distinguished from other failures.
